name: DARWIN
full_name: DARk matter WImp search with liquid xenoN
summary: DARWIN was an R&D programme for a liquid-xenon dark-matter and rare-event observatory of several tens of tonnes. It later joined XENON and LZ teams to form XLZD. Its historical record is retained without counting DARWIN and XLZD as two completed detectors.
detection_principle: A proposed multitens-of-tonnes dual-phase liquid-xenon TPC would use S1/S2 and ultralow radioactive backgrounds to extend WIMP, neutrino and double-beta studies.

status.label: Multiple phases with different statuses
status.evidence: The University of Zurich states that DARWIN helped form the XLZD collaboration, formally established in September 2024.

collaboration.name: DARWIN Collaboration

key_parameters.name: Historical designed scale
key_parameters.value: Approximately 50-tonne-scale dual-phase xenon detector; distinguish total and active masses in different design versions.

phases.name: Incorporated into XLZD
phases.description: The common successor observatory has a separate record.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
